transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we finalize any arbitration strategy. I recently reconciled a late-produced onboarding export against our user-agreement database, and the numbers are significant: only 312 of the 480 putative class members have executed agreements containing an arbitration provision. The remaining 168 do not have arbitration clauses. I haven't yet incorporated this reconciliation into the arbitration analysis, but it obviously affects our ability to compel arbitration across the entire putative class.

transcript.text: Marisol, I can speak to the business constraints. This position has not yet been put into the litigation strategy memo, but it's an approved business decision and directly relevant to the limited injunction proposal and any response strategy you issue.

transcript.text: Evan, that's a critical finding. transcript.text: Thank you both. This is exactly why we do this alignment before I issue the binding strategy. Let me synthesize what I'm hearing: On the arbitration front, Evan's reconciliation means we can only compel arbitration for 312 of the 480 putative class members. The remaining 168 without arbitration clauses will stay in litigation regardless, so we're looking at a dual-track approach — arbitration motions for the covered users and continued litigation defense for the uncovered users. On the business side, Talia's update is very helpful. The client's decision to withdraw all referral-related marketing claims within 60 days without admitting wrongdoing aligns directly with our limited injunction proposal and gives us a concrete corrective action to present to the court. That should help narrow the scope of what's genuinely in dispute. Before I issue the binding response strategy, are there any other discovery developments or business constraints I need to factor in? If not, I'll draft the strategy to reflect: (1) arbitration motions scoped to the 312 users with executed arbitration provisions, (2) continued litigation for the 168 without, (3) a limited injunction proposal framed around the client's 60-day marketing claims withdrawal, and (4) no admission of wrongdoing.
